events.title: Watson and Crick Announce the Structure of DNA
events.description: Francis Crick and James Watson, working at the Cavendish Laboratory in Cambridge, determined the double helix structure of DNA and reportedly announced they had found the 'secret of life' at the Eagle pub. Their model drew on X-ray diffraction data from Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins. The formal paper was published in Nature in April 1953.
events.significance: The discovery of DNA's double helix structure laid the foundation for modern molecular biology, genetics, and biotechnology, enabling advances such as genetic engineering, forensic DNA analysis, and the Human Genome Project.

events.title: Accra Crossroads Shooting Sparks Gold Coast Unrest
events.description: British colonial police fired on a march of ex-servicemen in Accra, Gold Coast (now Ghana), killing three veterans. The shooting triggered widespread riots and looting in Accra and other towns, and the colonial government arrested leaders of the United Gold Coast Convention.
events.significance: The unrest accelerated the movement toward self-rule and elevated Kwame Nkrumah, leading to Ghana becoming the first sub-Saharan African colony to gain independence in 1957.

events.title: Assassination of Swedish Prime Minister Olof Palme
events.description: Olof Palme was shot and killed on a Stockholm street while walking home from a cinema with his wife, Lisbet, who was wounded. The murder happened without bodyguards present. Despite one of the largest investigations in history, the case remained unsolved for decades, and prosecutors closed it in 2020 naming Stig Engström as the likely culprit.
events.significance: The killing shocked Sweden, shattering its image as a safe, open society, and became one of the most famous unsolved political assassinations of the 20th century.

events.title: Start of the Waco Siege
events.description: Agents of the U.S. Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms attempted to raid the Branch Davidian compound near Waco, Texas, to serve weapons warrants on leader David Koresh. A firefight killed four agents and six Davidians, beginning a 51-day standoff with the FBI that ended on April 19 in a fire that killed about 76 people.
events.significance: The siege became a flashpoint in debates over federal law enforcement tactics and religious freedom, and it influenced anti-government extremism, including the 1995 Oklahoma City bombing.

events.title: Wallace Carothers Invents Nylon
events.description: Chemist Wallace Carothers and his team at DuPont created nylon 6,6, the first fully synthetic fiber, in their laboratory in Wilmington, Delaware. Nylon was introduced commercially in the late 1930s, notably in stockings and later military uses such as parachutes.
events.significance: Nylon transformed the textile and materials industries and opened the era of synthetic polymers that now underpin countless consumer and industrial products.
